analysis.material_system: Graphite-based negative electrode (anode) blended with a minor fraction of a higher-Z, angular silicon-based additive, most likely SiOx or micro-Si, possibly carbon-coated. Evidence: about 70-75% of the section is low-Z particles (dark grey in BSE) shaped as flakes or potatoes, 5-20 um across, with lamellar internal texture and basal-plane cleavage cracks, which is typical of graphite. About 5-6% of the area is BSE-bright (clearly higher mean Z than carbon), compact, angular/faceted 2-7 um particles of the kind used as SiOx/Si capacity additives. The carbon-binder domain is sparse (thin films plus small carbon-black clusters), as expected for a water-processed graphite anode. No current collector or electrode surface is in view. The element identity of the bright phase cannot be confirmed without EDS. Shells around, and porosity inside, some bright particles hint at a cycled electrode but do not prove it.

phases.name: Graphite (active material)
phases.identification_evidence: Majority phase at the carbon BSE level. Flake/lens and rounded potato shapes with lamellar internal texture, basal-plane slits and fold boundaries decorated with nanopores, characteristic of flake/spheroidized graphite.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: uniform dark grey, at the same level as CBD/binder; thin slightly brighter outlines at edges; internal slits show as dark lines. Inlens: dark to medium grey with strong tone differences between and within particles (orientation/surface-state and charging contrast), streaky lamellae and bright crack edges. SE: flat mid grey with fine inclined milling striations; internal cracks are clear.
phases.morphology: Flakes/lens-shaped platelets (long axis 5-20 um, thickness 2-8 um, aspect ratio ~2-4) and large rounded potato particles up to ~20 um (e.g. top centre x~79-100 um, y~5-21 um; right x~149-168 um, y~28-44 um). Many flakes are split along basal planes. Long axes are mostly near-horizontal with +/-30-45 deg scatter. Thinner, splintered flakes dominate the left third.

phases.name: Si-based additive (SiOx or Si), dense angular particles
phases.identification_evidence: Much brighter than graphite in BSE, so clearly higher mean Z than carbon. Blocky, faceted shapes with sharp fracture edges, 2-7 um, ~5% of area; this matches milled SiOx/Si additives in graphite anodes. Si cannot be distinguished from SiOx (or another Z~10-14 phase) without EDS.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: bright and homogeneous apart from shot noise; many have a 0.3-1 um darker (lower-Z) shell. Inlens: medium-bright with fine granular internal texture and bright rims; charging streaks on some. SE: lighter than graphite (material contrast) and carrying the strongest milling striations in the image.
phases.morphology: Compact angular shards/polyhedra, aspect ratio 1-2, equivalent diameter mostly 3-7 um plus 1-2 um fragments. They sit in pockets between graphite flakes, with mild clustering at x~46-60 um, y~7-19 um and x~100-112 um, y~22-50 um.

phases.name: Mottled/porous Si-rich particles (sub-population)
phases.identification_evidence: BSE-bright but with lower mean intensity and dark sub-um internal spots, and a spongy texture in Inlens; distinct from the homogeneous angular particles.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: intermediate-bright, speckled with dark spots. Inlens: bright, foam/bubble-like texture. SE: rough, granular surface.
phases.morphology: Irregular rounded-to-angular aggregates 2-6 um, e.g. x~143-148 um, y~27-33 um; x~11-17 um, y~36-42 um; x~143-148 um, y~5-7 um; x~114-117 um, y~28-30 um. They could be cycling-degraded porous SiOx, Si/C composite or nano-Si agglomerates; this cannot be determined here.

phases.name: Carbon-binder domain and surface films (carbon black + binder, possibly SEI)
phases.identification_evidence: Fine-grained, fluffy material in interstices and on pore floors, plus conformal films along particle surfaces. Strongly SE-emissive in Inlens; carbon-like BSE level with granular texture.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: dark grey, marginally lighter than graphite, as fine granular patches (e.g. x~60-64 um, y~23-26 um; x~81-83 um, y~29-33 um); thin bright rims on particles. Inlens: very bright cauliflower-like carbon-black clusters, and smooth, concentrically banded charging films wrapping particles (e.g. x~96-103 um, y~29-33 um; x~107-114 um, y~25-28 um). SE: fuzzy texture, often recessed on pore floors.
phases.morphology: Films ~0.1-0.5 um thick on most particle surfaces; discrete clusters 0.5-3 um in gaps and triple junctions. Smooth banded domains are of uncertain nature (binder-rich CBD, thick SEI or resin). Part of the granular area is recessed and actually belongs to pore space in the section plane.

phases.name: Pores (open, not resin-filled)
phases.identification_evidence: Black in BSE and SE. SE and Inlens show depth, sidewalls and subsurface particles inside, so the pores are open.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: black where deep, grey where subsurface material is exposed. Inlens: dark with bright rims and visible material at depth. SE: black recesses with visible sidewalls and fuzzy CBD on the floors.
phases.morphology: Slit-like/lenticular interflake gaps 0.5-3 um wide and 3-40 um long, aligned with flake long axes (near-horizontal). A few equiaxed 2-4 um voids at flake junctions; sub-um voids in the CBD.

porosity.character: Dominated by slit-shaped, near-horizontally aligned interflake gaps (0.5-3 um wide, up to ~40 um long), plus small polygonal voids at flake junctions and sub-um porosity in the CBD. Pores are concentrated in two areas: a mid-height band in the centre (y~21-23 um, x~80-122 um, including one nearly continuous ~40 um gap) and the lower-left quadrant (x~0-48 um, y~33-44 um). The upper-left and upper-right are dense. In 2D the slits link through CBD-filled necks, suggesting a connected in-plane network, but 3D connectivity and tortuosity cannot be judged from a single section.
porosity.comment: The 9.8% pore class matches the deep black gaps fairly well. Adding recessed pore floors, which are grey in BSE but visibly below the polished plane in SE, gives ~12-15% open in-plane porosity. Even this is a lower bound: CBD nanoporosity is below resolution, and smooth binder/film domains count as solid. Any resin would also count as solid, since epoxy has nearly the same BSE level as graphite. Calendered graphite anodes are typically 25-35% porous, so either this region is strongly densified or much porosity is not captured; this cannot be resolved from these images.

analysis.binder_carbon_network: Sparse-to-moderate and mostly film-like. Most graphite and Si-rich particle surfaces carry a thin (~0.1-0.5 um) continuous film that is edge-bright in Inlens (binder and/or SEI), often with a serrated outline. Discrete carbon-black/binder clusters are small (0.5-3 um) and occur in interflake gaps, triple junctions and on pore floors: fluffy and granular in Inlens, fine-grained and marginally lighter in BSE. They are more frequent around Si-rich particles and along the central pore band than in the dense upper-left. Smooth, charging-bright, concentrically banded deposits wrap several Si-rich particles (x~96-104 um, y~29-33 um; x~107-114 um, y~25-28 um); binder accumulation or thick SEI is plausible, and resin cannot be excluded. Carbon-black percolation between particles looks patchy, so electronic contact likely relies largely on direct graphite-graphite contacts (interpretation). BSE cannot separate CBD from graphite, so the ~9% CBD fraction is a visual estimate based on Inlens.
analysis.particle_packing_and_alignment: Dense, imbricated packing of graphite flakes with extensive face-to-face contacts and little open space apart from slit pores; the in-plane solid fraction is ~85-88%. Flake long axes are preferentially near-horizontal (most within +/-30-40 deg), and the slit pores share this orientation, consistent with calendering. Vertical is therefore most likely the through-thickness direction (medium confidence; no current collector or free surface is visible to confirm). The left third contains more steeply inclined, splintered thin flakes, while the centre and right contain larger rounded particles up to ~20 um. Si-rich particles sit in pockets between flakes, touching graphite on several sides but often separated by a thin shell or gap.

heterogeneity.description: Moderate. Composition is broadly uniform: Si-rich particles appear across the full width at ~5 per 1000 um2, with mild clusters at x~46-60 um, y~7-19 um and x~100-112 um, y~22-50 um. Pore distribution is uneven: a mid-height slit band in the centre and a porous lower-left zone contrast with a dense upper-left and upper-right. Particle size and shape also vary laterally, with fragmented thin flakes on the left and large potato particles in the centre and right.

defects_and_damage.description: Thin slit cracks/delaminations along basal planes inside many graphite flakes (e.g. a ~4 um slit at x~78-82 um, y~23 um), plus multiply split, splintered flakes. Possible causes are calendering, preparation or cycling; the images cannot distinguish them.
defects_and_damage.location: Throughout; most frequent in the left third (x~0-60 um)

defects_and_damage.type: interparticle slit gaps / separation of flake stacks
defects_and_damage.description: A near-continuous horizontal gap ~1-2 um wide runs over ~40 um between flake layers, with similar gaps in the lower left. These reduce local contact between flake stacks; they may be partly calendering spring-back and partly sectioning-induced.
defects_and_damage.location: Centre, mid-height (x~80-122 um, y~21-23 um); lower-left (x~0-48 um, y~33-44 um)

defects_and_damage.description: Branched, dendritic network of fine cracks inside a large (~19 x 15 um) rounded graphite particle.
defects_and_damage.location: Right side, lower half (x~149-155 um, y~34-38 um)

defects_and_damage.type: shells / partial debonding around Si-rich particles
defects_and_damage.description: Many bright particles are surrounded by a 0.3-1 um lower-BSE shell and locally by narrow gaps to the matrix. The shell is thicker than a typical CVD carbon coating; it may be a reaction/SEI shell or a binder layer, and it indicates imperfect particle-matrix contact. A pair of closely stacked bright fragments may be one particle fractured during calendering.
defects_and_damage.location: Several, e.g. x~103-111 um, y~33-42 um and x~54-60 um, y~12-19 um

defects_and_damage.description: A few bright particles have a spongy, speckled interior. Possible explanations are lithiation-induced porosity/pulverization or an intrinsically porous composite.
Saw-tooth surface layers ~0.2-0.5 um thick along many graphite edges. They could be exfoliated edge planes, SEI/binder films or a milling effect.
defects_and_damage.location: Widespread, e.g. lower edge of the top-centre potato particle (x~83-100 um, y~18-21 um)

imaging_artifacts.description: Horizontal scan streaks and smeared bright patches on and near Si-rich particles and smooth films (e.g. x~102-104 um, y~24-27 um; right frame edge x~170-175 um, y~26-31 um). Smooth films also show brightness gradients and concentric banding.

Fine inclined striations across polished surfaces in SE (faint in Inlens), strongest on the harder Si-rich particles (e.g. x~54-60 um, y~12-19 um). They suggest ion-beam (likely BIB) preparation; no smearing of graphite into pores is seen.
Pores are open, so subsurface particles and CBD are imaged on pore floors. In BSE these regions are grey rather than black, so the threshold assigns part of the pore area to solid.
Strong edge brightening outlines every particle and crack, inflating the apparent CBD/film area in Inlens.
Speckle inside bright particles and graininess in graphite. This fragments bright objects and roughens pore boundaries in the threshold.
Isolated tiny dark dashes (line dropouts) in BSE and Inlens (e.g. x~83 um, y~43 um; x~97 um, y~25 um), and a thin dark band along part of the bottom-right edge of the Inlens frame.

detector_insights.BSE: Best channel for separating phases by Z. Si-rich particles are unambiguous (bright), and BSE reveals their internal state (homogeneous vs mottled) and lower-Z shells. Graphite, carbon black, binder and any epoxy (mean Z ~6) are almost identical in grey level, so the CBD can only be inferred from subtle granular texture, and the threshold's middle class lumps these phases together. Pores read black only where deep; grey pore floors cause under-counting. Thin brighter rims on graphite may be binder/SEI films or an edge effect.
detector_insights.Inlens: Most informative for the CBD and surfaces: carbon-black clusters, films and edges appear bright. It shows lamellar texture and tone differences between graphite particles that are invisible in BSE (orientation, surface damage, two graphite grades or uneven Li content; undeterminable). It also shows fine granular texture in dense Si-rich particles, spongy texture in the porous ones, and smooth banded deposits around Si-rich particles. It is the channel most affected by charging streaks, gradients and edge brightening, so it is unsuitable for direct thresholding.
detector_insights.ETD_or_SE: Topographic channel. It confirms that black regions are open, deep pores (sidewalls and subsurface particles visible) rather than resin-filled. It shows ion-milling striations and particle cracks clearly, and Si-rich particles appear lighter through material contrast. It shows slightly more dark/recessed pore area than BSE, supporting the view that the BSE pore class is conservative.

analysis.threshold_metrics_assessment: Pore area (9.8%) is roughly consistent with the deep black slit pores (visual ~10%) but biased low as a measure of porosity. Grey recessed pore floors, sub-resolution CBD pores and BSE-graphite-like binder/film (or resin) domains are all counted as solid; I estimate ~13% open in-plane porosity. Bright raw (6.3%) slightly overestimates the Si-rich phase because thin bright rims, CBD patches near threshold 83 and noise pixels are included. Bright particle area (5.1%) is trustworthy to about +/-1.5 points (visual estimate 5-6%), though mottled particles may be partly lost. The count (50; 5.5 per 1000 um2) is plausible (~40-45 discrete particles visible) but slightly inflated by fragmentation. The median equivalent diameter (2.49 um) is biased low, because 1-3 um fragments dominate the number statistic while the main angular population is ~4-6 um. The p90 (5.27 um) is about right to slightly low. No graphite or CBD metric can be derived from this BSE threshold.
notable_features: Blend of graphite flakes/potato particles with ~5-6% area of bright angular Si-based particles
Many Si-rich particles have 0.3-1 um lower-Z shells (core-shell look), thicker than a typical carbon coating
Small sub-population of bright particles with spongy/porous interiors (possible cycling degradation or composite particles)
Smooth, charging-bright, concentrically banded deposits wrap several Si-rich particles in Inlens (binder, SEI or resin; undetermined)
Pronounced Inlens tone variation among graphite particles that is absent in BSE
Near-continuous ~40 um horizontal slit pore at mid-height in the centre; slit pores generally aligned with flakes
Fold boundaries in large rounded graphite decorated with chains of nanopores (e.g. x~98-100 um, y~10-14 um)
Branched crack network in a large graphite particle at x~149-155 um, y~34-38 um
No current collector or electrode surface in view; through-thickness direction inferred only from flake alignment
analysis.summary: This is a graphite-dominated anode containing ~5-6% (area) of bright, angular 2-7 um Si-based additive particles (most likely SiOx/Si; composition unconfirmed), in a densely packed network of graphite flakes and potato-shaped particles whose long axes lie mostly horizontally (vertical is probably through-thickness). The carbon-binder domain is sparse, consisting of thin films on particle surfaces plus small carbon-black clusters, and is visible mainly in Inlens because it matches graphite in BSE. Visible porosity (~13%) consists of slit-like interflake gaps concentrated in a central mid-height band and the lower left; graphite basal-plane cracks, shells around Si-rich particles and a few porous Si-rich particles may indicate cycling, though this cannot be confirmed. The automatic BSE bright-phase area (5.1-6.3%) is credible, but its median particle size is biased low and the 9.8% pore fraction should be treated as a lower bound.
